tool.name: AHP-OS (AHP Online System) - AHP Priority Calculator
tool.version: ahp-calc.php Rev 172, last update 2022-02-26 (from the page footer; AHP-OS does not display a global version number)

captured.notes: Model building and judgment entry were automated in the operator's browser; every entered judgment was read back from the form and checked against the fixture before calculation, and the outputs were transcribed verbatim from the results page (see the transcript artifact). The operator manually checked the session and outputs before this capture was committed. The calculator is publicly accessible; no login was used.

drinks.notes: Priorities are displayed as percentages to one decimal (17.7%, 1.9%, 4.2%, 11.6%, 19.0%, 12.9%, 32.7%) and transcribed as fractions. CR is displayed as '2.2%'. CI is not displayed. The tool also displays per-priority uncertainty estimates ('(+)'/'(-)' columns) and an 'Eigenvector solution: 4 iterations, delta = 2.4E-8' line, which have no counterpart in the fixture.

ri_table.name: other
ri_table.source: Confirmed from the published source code (github.com/bpmsg/ahp-os, classes/AhpCalc.php): the function setAlonsoCr() computes CR = (lambda_max - n) / ((2.7699*n - 4.3513) - n), citing Alonso & Lamata (2006), and the priority calculator page (ahp-calc.php) displays exactly this value (cr_alo). The same class also contains setSaatyCr() with a classic-style RI table (0.57, 0.9, 1.12, 1.24, 1.32, ...), but that value is not the one the calculator displays. The documented formula is also stated in K. D. Goepel, 'Implementation of an online software tool for the analytic hierarchy process (AHP-OS)', IJAHP 10(3), 2018 (working-paper eq. 2.5). The values given here are the effective RI(n) = (1.7699*n - 4.3513)/(n - 1) implied by the formula; the displayed CRs of all captured matrices reproduce under it (n=7: 0.0220 -> '2.2%'; n=4: 0.0201 -> '2.0%'; n=5: 0.0919 -> '9.2%'). Note this linear-fit variant differs slightly from the Alonso-Lamata Table 1 values used by the fixture ri-table-alonso-lamata (e.g. 0.9094 vs 0.8815 at n=4).

matrices.drinks.priorities.note: The displayed percentages equal the fixture's published expected priorities exactly at the tool's display precision (three decimal places as fractions).

matrices.drinks.lambda_max.note: Tool displays 7.177 (three decimals); expected derived value is 7.176629. Tolerance reflects the display precision.

matrices.drinks.cr.note: Displayed '2.2%' equals the fixture's published CR 0.022. The tool computes CR with the Alonso-Lamata linear fit (see ri_table), which gives 0.0220 here; the fixture's Saaty (1980) table gives 0.0223. Both display as 2.2% and both are within the fixture's tolerance of the published value.

reverify.instructions: Open https://bpmsg.com/ahp/ahp-calc.php (no account needed). Enter 7 as the number of criteria and click Go; name them Coffee, Wine, Tea, Beer, Sodas, Milk, Water and click OK. Enter the 21 pairwise judgments from the fixture's matrix (upper triangle, row by row; for entries below 1, select the second element and the reciprocal intensity - e.g. Coffee vs Water 1/2 means selecting Water with intensity 2; the full list is in the transcript artifact). Click 'Check Consistency' / 'Calculate'. The results section shows the priorities, 'Consistency Ratio CR' and 'Principal eigen value' transcribed here. The result can also be exported with the 'Download_(.csv)' button.
